title: Fixed-effort trawl richness had opposite temperature links in early Northeast and late Bering samples in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested seasonal sea-surface temperature links to recorded taxon richness in eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US fall trawls in 1982-2019. An exact draw calculation fixed effort at one haul per stratum in each year. Four region-period models controlled linear year. The early Northeast slope was 6.69 expected taxa per C, with a four-test interval of 2.96 to 10.41. The later Bering slope was -3.54, with an interval of -5.64 to -1.45. The other intervals included zero. Two-haul, covariance-lag, persistent-list and consecutive-year checks kept the two clear signs. The links therefore did not show a common stable response across regions and periods. Fixed effort removes direct haul-count variation, but not detection, gear, identification or spatial sampling changes. Coarse surface temperature and short series limit inference. These are survey associations, not causal climate effects. We did not measure pollution or ecological timing. Code, sufficient evidence, raw source hashes, uncertainty and independent checks are included.

display.caption: Recorded richness, exact fixed-effort richness, and temperature slopes in two regions and two periods. Intervals adjust for four primary tests. Regional richness levels have different sample-size targets.
